# Example llms.txt — STATIC SAMPLE, NOT AUTO-GENERATED
#
# The plugin used to generate llms.txt automatically; that feature was removed
# in 1.3.x (along with the `--with-llmstxt` WP-CLI flag). This file is a hand-
# authored template you can adapt and place at your web root: https://example.org/llms.txt
#
# Why have one: it serves "go straight to the Markdown" agents (Pattern B in
# ../README.md) a single site-level index, independent of User-Agent matching or
# cache configuration. Every link below points at the cache-safe, WAF-friendly
# `?output_format=md` route — the route we stand behind.
#
# Trade-off to weigh before reintroducing auto-generation: a manifest must be
# kept in sync with published/retired content (stale entries point agents at
# 404s), and on a large site it is large. The discovery `<link rel="alternate">`
# tag in each page's <head> already covers Pattern A without a manifest.
#
# Format follows the emerging llms.txt convention: an H1 site name, an optional
# blockquote summary, then H2 sections of `- [Title](url): note` links.

# Example Org

> One-line description of the site and what an agent will find here.

## Core pages

- [About](https://example.org/about/?output_format=md): who we are and what we do
- [Our impact](https://example.org/our-impact/?output_format=md): outcomes and figures
- [Get involved](https://example.org/get-involved/?output_format=md): ways to take part
